decisions.reason: After several years with no visible market follow-through, this niche particle-therapy phantom looks like a higher-cost option whose uncertainty has largely resolved without enough evidence of broad uptake.
A small-volume ionization chamber remains close to the firm's core dosimetry business and is relatively inexpensive to keep available while serving specialist demand.
Given prolonged low visibility and likely overlap with other chamber offerings, this chamber's option value now appears weaker than the benefit of simplifying the portfolio.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with multiple models fits routine customer workflows and the firm's established calibration and service capabilities, so it is still worth retaining.
This relative-dosimetry chamber is specialized but still complements the firm's measurement portfolio and likely costs little to keep on the market.
Although somewhat overlapping with other chambers, a thimble chamber is a familiar core-category product and still has enough residual option value to justify keeping it for now.
